### Q1
No, the JSON file store stays. Ops backs up `data/store.json` with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary SQLite file would break their backup checks. Instead we debounced the writes (200 ms) in `src/store.ts`.

### Q2
Yes, `src/legacy/`. It is vendored from the old logistics monolith, and the platform team's sync job overwrites the folder every Monday, so any change there is silently lost.

### Q3
It goes into the JSON body as a top-level `sig` field, computed (HMAC-SHA256, hex) over the JSON body without `sig`. We first sent it in an `X-Signature` header, but the ERP's API gateway strips every custom X- header, so the signature never arrived and the ERP rejected everything as unsigned.

### Q4
Port 9911. The docs and README still say 8080, which is outdated since the October infra move. The ERP team owns the doc, and you said you'd fix the README yourself. `config/default.json` still has 8080 as of my last look.

### Q5
New user-facing `message` texts must be in German, because the warehouse staff UI shows them verbatim to the packers. The `code` field stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Older existing messages are still English.

### Q6
Through a hardcoded list of Austrian public holidays for 2026 and 2027 in `src/services/holidays.ts`, which `isBusinessDay` in `eta.ts` consults. It is hardcoded because the warehouse deployment has no outbound internet access, so a holiday API is not an option.

### Q7
No. The ERP answers 422 to any array payload and only accepts a single event object per request, as you found when you tried it in September. So we don't build batching.

### Q8
No new npm packages, neither runtime nor dev dependencies. Every new package has to go through the security review, which currently takes about six weeks.

### Q9
Not in this repo. I measured it and found that `calculateEta` costs only about 0.2 ms for 50 items and 2.5 ms for 500, so I did not build it. You then said QA found a stale-ETA bug from a memoization (no invalidation after a new event), and that caching ETAs is a dead end. I found no such code here, so it must come from a version I haven't seen.

### Q10
At most 3 attempts in total, with a fixed 30-second delay between them and no exponential backoff. The ERP only deduplicates by `event_id` within a 2-minute window, so all attempts must land inside it or we create duplicates. I retry only network errors and 5xx, not 4xx.

### Q11
The recipient's name, address and phone number must never be logged, because it is personal data under GDPR and the data protection officer flagged exactly this in last month's audit. Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine to log.

### Q12
Yes, `emits webhook on delivered` in `test/events.test.ts`, known as OPS-412. It fails about 1 in 5 CI runs because of a timer race in the fake notifier. If it fails, rerun once and don't try to fix it, because the platform team owns the fix.

### Q13
Only ATP numbers are validated, as UPU S10 (2 letters, 8 digits, check digit, `AT`) with the check digit algorithm from `docs/carriers.md`. All other carriers accept any non-empty value, because their formats change too often and last year valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for two days.

### Q14
`fs.watch` never fires on staging, because the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and the file change events don't propagate into the container. `fs.watchFile` (polling) worked. Nothing has been built for it yet.

### Q15
Yes, `GET /shipments/:id`. The mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields, and the next release isn't until January. That's why `eta` went only into the list endpoint, and a test pins the exact field set.
